title: Unique lifting of maps from completions into a henselian target
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $D$ a finite type commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Suppose $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian $A$-algebra such that $(C,IC)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Write $D^\wedge=\varprojlim_nD/I^nD$ and $C^\wedge=\varprojlim_n C/I^nC$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Every $A$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:D^\wedge\to C^\wedge$ is the completion of a unique $A$-algebra homomorphism $u:D\to C$. Equivalently, composition with $C\to C^\wedge$ sends $u$ to the restriction of $\varphi$ along $D\to D^\wedge$; the completion of $u$ equals $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ (lemma-fully-faithful-etale-over-complement), specialized to a henselian target, whose pair henselization is itself. All algebra homomorphisms of completions are I-adically continuous, since they preserve I^n.

proof.text: Write $\iota_M:M\to M^\wedge$ for the completion map. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete], applied over $A$ to $M=D,C$, the projections to $M/I^nM$ are onto with kernels $I^nM^\wedge$. The ideal $I$ is finitely generated because $A$ is Noetherian. An $A$-algebra map between these completions sends $I^nD^\wedge$ into $I^nC^\wedge$, hence is continuous and induces maps $\varphi_n:D/I^nD\to C/I^nC$. For $x\in D^\wedge$ choose $d_n\in D$ representing its $n$th coordinate. Then $x-\iota_D(d_n)\in I^nD^\wedge$, so the $n$th coordinate of $\varphi(x)$ equals $\varphi_n(d_n)$. Thus $\varphi$ is exactly the inverse limit of these quotient maps and is determined by its restriction to $D$. The same argument shows that an $A$-algebra map $u:D\to C$ has the required completion if and only if $\iota_Cu=\varphi\iota_D$.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ, interpretation of maps of completions; algebra.tex Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated).

proof.text: Set $E=D\otimes_A C$ and $J=IC$. A finite algebra generating list for $D$ gives the generators $d_i\otimes1$ for $E$ over $C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $E$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale off $V(J)$: this is the inverse image of the given etale restriction. At level $n$, the balanced rule $d\otimes c\mapsto\varphi_n(d\bmod I^nD)(c\bmod J^n)$ defines $E/J^nE\to C/J^n$. These maps commute with reductions. Their inverse limit is $\sigma:E^\wedge\to C^\wedge$. It retracts the structural map $C^\wedge\to E^\wedge$, coordinate by coordinate, so is a $C^\wedge$-algebra map and is surjective. On $D$ it is $\varphi\iota_D$.

Apply [lem-per-completed-retraction-conormal-torsion] with $R=C$, ideal $J$ and algebra $S=E$ to get $J^c(K/K^2)=0$ for $K=\ker\sigma$. We need algebraization retaining the map out of $E$. Apply [lem-per-conormal-torsion-algebraization] with its base ring and its finite type algebra BOTH equal to $E$, and its ideal equal to $JE$. The identity makes $E$ finite type over itself, and $(JE)^c$ annihilates the same conormal module. It yields a finite type $E$-algebra $T$ and an $E$-algebra isomorphism $\beta:T^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}C^\wedge$, where the $E$-structure on $C^\wedge$ is $\sigma\iota_E$. Both completions here are for $J$. Generators for $E$ over $C$ followed by generators for $T$ over $E$ show that $T$ is finite type over $C$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes it Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ, conormal annihilation and application of more-algebra.tex Tag 0ALR (lemma-quotient-by-idempotent).

proof.text: The map $\beta$ is $C$-linear and therefore preserves the powers of $J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete], for each $n\geq1$ it induces an isomorphism $T/J^nT\cong C/J^n$. Its composite with the structural map $C/J^n\to T/J^nT$ is the identity, since $\beta$ is an $E$-algebra map and $\sigma$ is a retraction. Consequently that structural map is itself an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-infinitesimal-neighbourhoods] to $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$. Both affine schemes are Noetherian and the map is finite type. Every infinitesimal restriction is an isomorphism, hence etale. We obtain an etale open $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}T$ containing $V(JT)$.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ, etaleness near V(I); more-morphisms.tex Tag 0A43 (lemma-check-smoothness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds), part (2).

proof.text: Write the closed complement of $W$ as $V(L)$ for an ideal $L\subseteq T$. Since $V(L)\cap V(JT)$ is empty, $L+JT=T$. Choose $g\in L$ with $g=1-a$, $a\in JT$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}T_g=D(g)\subseteq W$. The inclusion into $W$ is open, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], parts (1),(2), shows that $C\to T_g$ is etale. Modulo $J^n$ the element $g$ is invertible, with inverse $1+a+\cdots+a^{n-1}$; hence $T_g/J^nT_g=T/J^nT$. Thus localization has not changed the completion or any of the structural quotient isomorphisms. Put $F=T_g$, and retain the isomorphism $\beta:F^\wedge\to C^\wedge$. The algebra $F$ is finite type over $C$, generated by generators of $T$ and $g^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ, replacement by a localization without changing completion; the etale-near-closed-fibre open suffices for the henselian target specialization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-stage-map] to the etale map $C\to F$ with $C/J\cong F/JF$, and the identity morphism into the henselian pair $(C,J)$. It gives a unique $C$-algebra map $\tau:F\to C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete], $C^\wedge$ is complete for $J$; the filtration by the extended ideal $JC^\wedge$ has the same powers. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian] makes $(C^\wedge,JC^\wedge)$ henselian. Apply the uniqueness clause of the same stage-map node with target $C^\wedge$. Both $\iota_C\tau$ and $\beta\iota_F$ extend $\iota_C:C\to C^\wedge$, and the ideal condition holds by construction. They are therefore equal. Define $u$ as the composite $D\to E\to T\to F\xrightarrow{\tau}C$. The $E$-linearity of $\beta$ gives $\iota_Cu=\sigma\iota_E|_D=\varphi\iota_D$. Step 1 shows that the completion of $u$ is exactly $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ, last sentence; more-algebra.tex Tags 0A02 (lemma-henselization), final paragraph, and 0ALJ (lemma-complete-henselian).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion], henselianity of $(C,J)$ implies $J\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(C)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] to the Noetherian ring $C$ and the finite module $M=C$, generated by $1$. It gives $\bigcap_{n\geq1}J^n=0$, so $\iota_C:C\to C^\wedge$ is injective: its kernel consists exactly of elements lying in all these powers. If $u,v:D\to C$ have the specified completion, Step 1 gives $\iota_Cu=\varphi\iota_D=\iota_Cv$; injectivity gives $u(d)=v(d)$ for each $d$. This proves uniqueness and completes both formulations of the statement.

source.place: Tag 0AKJ, uniqueness paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tag 09XI and algebra.tex Tag 00IQ.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0AKJ (lemma-fully-faithful-etale-over-complement); specialized henselian target. The etale-near-closed-fibre open is localized directly, since global etaleness away from V(I) of the algebraized section is unnecessary for this specialization.
